subject: Every inline Code and HTML node's position, compared with cmark-gfm's own --sourcepos over the CommonMark spec fixture.
purpose:
Nine rows, and for the first time in this ledger's life they are rows where THIS SIDE IS RIGHT. It read zero for the whole of Stage 0a: every inline position agreed with cmark-gfm's, including the ones that were wrong, which is exactly what specs/positions/places.json's closing note says this oracle cannot see.

   6  raw-html-loses-its-closing-byte   `a <b` / `c> d` gives a raw-HTML node whose literal ends at 2:2 and whose scope ended at 2:1, so its closing `>` belonged to no node at all. places.json names this input, pins it as a golden row in regression.txt, and assigns it to Step 8. Step 8's projection closes it: an inline node's extent is a projection of the byte range it covers, and asking the content-to-source map where the last byte is answers 2:2. Upstream still reports 2:1 on all six.
   3  multi-line-span-ends-at-a-line-ending   A code span crossing a line ending now ends at the end of the line its last byte is on -- `1:3..2:4` -- where upstream says column 0 of the line after -- `1:3..3:0`. Both are line-ending spellings; this one names the right line. See places.json's family of the same name and Q45.

AGREEING WITH AN AUTHORITY THAT IS ITSELF WRONG IS NOT AGREEMENT. This ledger's value was always that it would go non-zero the moment this engine's inline positions stopped being cmark-gfm's; what it did not say until now is that the first such moment would be an improvement. A row here is a disagreement, not a defect, and each one's closedBy says which.
